step2.ptxt: CAN communication malfunction codes are also output due to internal malfunctions and power supply malfunctions of ECUs and sensors in systems that use CAN communication, so pay attention if internal malfunction or power supply malfunction codes for the system concerned are output or stored at the same time.

If a CAN communication malfunction code is confirmed, or if there is no response to SST (TaSCAN) from an ECU that outputs via CAN communication, first check that the DLC3 branch wire and main bus main line circuits are normal.
By inspecting the DLC3 terminals using SST (Toyota electrical tester), malfunctions in the DLC3 branch wire and CAN V bus main line circuits can be checked.

item.ptxt: When inspecting the DLC3 connector, do not insert the tester probes directly; connect SST (diagnosis check wire No.2 (09843-18040)) to inspect.
Open circuits in the branch wires of each ECU (sensor) and the V bus No.2 and MS bus circuits cannot be inspected from DLC3.

step2.ptxt: By checking "CAN Bus Connected ECU" using SST (TaSCAN), ECUs (sensors) with open branch wires connected to the CAN bus circuit can be identified. (When DLC3 branch wire and main bus main line circuits are normal)

item.ptxt: When checking CAN bus connected ECUs, ECUs (sensors) with open branch wires do not respond to (are not displayed on) SST (TaSCAN).
When checking CAN bus connected ECUs, if all ECUs respond (are displayed) but a CAN communication malfunction DTC is output, check the communication malfunction DTCs.

step2.ptxt: For past V bus malfunctions, identify the ECU (sensor) whose communication was lost from the combination of communication malfunction DTCs output.
Malfunctions in the MS bus circuit are detected by the main body ECU, which outputs a DTC corresponding to the malfunctioning area.
Malfunctions in the V bus No.2 circuit are detected by the CAN gateway ECU, which outputs a DTC corresponding to the malfunctioning area.

If an open circuit malfunction is confirmed, before disconnecting and inspecting the related connectors, push the connector case in the connecting direction and check that the connector is not loose or disconnected.
When disconnecting a connector, check that the connector terminals and connector case are free of damage, deformation, corrosion, etc.

atten3.ptxt: When measuring the resistance of the CAN bus, turn the IG OFF, confirm that warning functions such as the key reminder warning system are not operating, and leave the vehicle for 1 minutes or more without operating the key or opening/closing the doors before starting measurement. If it is necessary to open a door during inspection, open it beforehand.

descript-testgroup.testtitle: Customer Problem Analysis and Symptom Check

item.ptxt: If the ECU or sensor indicated by a CAN communication malfunction code as having lost communication has stored codes such as power supply malfunction or internal malfunction, it is highly likely that the ECU or sensor was unable to transmit signals rather than that the communication line is malfunctioning, so first troubleshoot the DTCs for those component malfunctions.

If a connector containing CAN communication lines is disconnected with the ignition ON or ACC ON, ECUs of related systems as well as the ECU of the system concerned store CAN communication malfunction codes.

descript-testgroup.testtitle: Check ECUs Connected to CAN Bus (Check Connection Status Using TaSCAN)

test1.ptxt: Display the "CAN Bus Diagnosis" → "CAN Bus Connected ECU Check" screen of SST (TaSCAN). (see )
Watch the screen display for approximately 1 minutes and check the display of connected ECUs (sensors).

entry.ptxt: No ECUs or sensors are displayed (MS bus malfunction codes U1002 and U0327 are output)
(V bus main line open or short malfunction, DLC3 branch line malfunction)
Main body ECU is displayed, but certification ECU is not displayed.
(MS bus main line open/short malfunction or certification ECU communication malfunction)
Main body ECU and certification ECU are not displayed.
(Main body ECU V bus connection branch line open)
None of the V bus No.2 connected ECUs except the CAN gateway ECU are displayed
(V bus No.2 main line open or short malfunction)
None of the ECUs connected to V bus No.2 are displayed
(CAN gateway ECU V bus connection branch line open)
1 of the ECUs or sensors that should be connected to CAN communication are not displayed on the screen
(ECU or sensor branch line open, communication stop)
Some of the ECUs and sensors that should be connected to CAN communication are not displayed on the screen, and some ECUs and sensors switch between displayed ←→ not displayed during the check
(ECU or sensor branch line open on one side)
All ECUs and sensors connected to CAN communication are displayed on the screen

atten3.ptxt: ECUs and sensors that are not installed are not displayed, so do not mistake them for ECUs or sensors with lost communication.

item.ptxt: If there is an ECU that switches between displayed ←→ not displayed during the check, an open on one side has occurred in the branch wire of one of the connected ECUs or sensors. (The signal of the ECU with the open on one side becomes noise and affects the response and display on TaSCAN.)

For MS bus connected ECUs, the ECUs with which the main body ECU has established communication are displayed on SST (TaSCAN), and for V bus No.2 connected ECUs, the ECUs with which the CAN gateway ECU has established communication are displayed. ECUs whose communication with the main body ECU or CAN gateway ECU has been lost for 10 seconds or more are no longer displayed on SST (TaSCAN).
For the communication lost mode of MS bus and V bus No.2 connected ECUs, refer to the flowchart of the DTC corresponding to the lost communication.

descript-testgroup.testtitle: Check Communication Malfunction DTCs (Check Past DTCs)

test1.ptxt: Perform "CAN Bus Diagnosis" → "Communication Malfunction DTC Check" on SST (TaSCAN). (see )
Record all codes stored in each ECU.

item.ptxt: If communication malfunction DTCs are stored and all ECUs and sensors connected to CAN communication are displayed on the TaSCAN "CAN Bus Connected ECU Check" screen, a past malfunction that is not currently occurring is suspected.
V bus branch wire malfunctions are detected by each related ECU, so identify the malfunctioning area from the combination of codes output.
For MS bus malfunctions, the main body ECU detects loss of communication with connected ECUs and network malfunctions, and outputs codes.
For V bus No.2 malfunctions, the CAN gateway ECU detects loss of communication with connected ECUs and outputs codes.
If V bus connected ECUs and the main body ECU or CAN gateway ECU are outputting malfunction codes, inspect and repair the MS bus and V bus No.2 first.
